There is a DLS query referencing a runtime field loaded from _source, when we create the collector manager we retrieve the numDocs which triggers going through all segments and executing the script for each document. StoredFieldSourceProvider relies on leaf ordinals to build an array, but those ordinals are not populated when computing the numDocs via BaseCompositeReader, as that goes through the subreaders contexts, and not the context leaves (there is a subtle difference that bites us there).

Fixes #111637
interesting, I did not even know this one existed, I would have used LeafReaderContext itself as a key, I've seen that done in other places too. But this should be fine as well
why not do a computeIfAbsent as opposed to get and then putIfAbsent?

reply.body: `computeIfAbsent` requires a capturing lambda here, since that lambda is mostly not used we can save a lot of cycles by using this approach. `computeIfAbsent` is also needlessly lock-heavy for our use-case. Since we know we will never really conflict here, there's no need for it's internal synchronisation on the key :)
and why then do a putIfAbsent and not just put if provider is null?
huh that's a fair point :) this should really be an assertion, thanks! Let me fix that :)

timeline.body: Can you rename to mention runtime fields but not runtime mappings? That is because runtime mappings may lead to runtime fields specified in the search request using the runtime_mappings section which is not what we do here.

I left some small comments, I also think that this is the right fix, at least until we introduce intra-segment concurrency. I don't think performance matters a lot here: when this is called as part of the query phase, we are already retrieving stored fields for every possible document, hence on a very slow path, using an array vs the updated approach won't make a lot of difference. It may make a bit of a difference in the fetch phase perhaps, but then again, the previous solution was relying on the false assumption that the ordinals are always correctly populated.


Could you update the description of the PR to explain the flow that leads to reproducing more clearly? There is a DLS query referencing a runtime field loaded from `_source`, when we create the collector manager we retrieve the numDocs which triggers going through all segments and executing the script for each document. StoredFieldSourceProvider relies on leaf ordinals to build an array, but those ordinals are not populated when computing the numDocs via BaseCompositeReader, as that goes through the subreaders contexts, and not the context leaves (there is a subtle difference that bites us there).

+===== Diagnosing other network disconnections
+
+{es} is designed to run on a fairly reliable network. It opens a number of TCP
+connections between nodes and expects these connections to remain open
+<<long-lived-connections,forever>>. If a connection is closed then {es} will
+try and reconnect, so the occasional blip may fail some in-flight operations
+but should otherwise have limited impact on the cluster. In contrast,
+repeatedly-dropped connections will severely affect its operation.
+
+{es} nodes will only actively close an outbound connection to another node if
+the other node leaves the cluster. See
+<<cluster-fault-detection-troubleshooting>> for further information about
+identifying and troubleshooting this situation. If an outbound connection
+closes for some other reason, nodes will log a message such as the following:
+
+[source,text]
+----
+[INFO ][o.e.t.ClusterConnectionManager] [node-1] transport connection to [{node-2}{g3cCUaMDQJmQ2ZLtjr-3dg}{10.0.0.1:9300}] closed by remote
+----
+
+Similarly, once an inbound connection is fully established, a node never
+spontaneously closes it unless the node is shutting down.
+
+Therefore if you see a node report that a connection to another node closed
+unexpectedly, something other than {es} likely caused the connection to close.
+A common cause is a misconfigured firewall with an improper timeout or another
+policy that's <<long-lived-connections,incompatible with {es}>>. It could also
+be caused by general connectivity issues, such as packet loss due to faulty
+hardware or network congestion. If you're an advanced user, configure the
+following loggers to get more detailed information about network exceptions:

+----

+network.
